reviewer: Pickle: official-source heated vest heating element, battery runtime and low-temperature burn safety comparison
method: Reviewed the full draft against official sources. Korea Consumer Agency heated vest comparative test (2021-01-18, policy briefing press release korea.kr newsId=156432392 plus Yonhap AKR20210118028600030): 10 products tested (Nepa Safety, Newjiro, Ttasumi, Black Yak, Swiss Military, Gero, K2, K2 Safety, Kolping, Treksta Safety); electrical appliance safety standard caps garment heating-surface temperature at 50 C (65 C for garments worn below freezing); 4 products exceeded it - Nepa Safety 52 C at stage 3, Swiss Military HIVE-310 55 C and 64 C at stages 2-3, K2 NAV 53 C and 57 C, Kolping 51 C and 63 C - and all four makers pledged voluntary recalls. Runtime measured: stage 1 average 32-47 C with 9-18 hours, stage 3 average 43-64 C with 4.5-10.5 hours; wash heating function normal for all, 4 products flagged for dye transfer; KCA guidance: wear over shirts/scarf so the heating panel never touches skin, stop use and seek care if pigmentation, red spots, itching or blisters appear (possible low-temperature burn). Low-temperature burn (policy briefing 2019-12-27, data by KCDC): 40-50 C exposure over long duration, blood circulation slows, heat accumulates, erythema/pigmentation/red spots/itching/blisters, can become 2nd-3rd degree burns reaching subcutaneous fat; children, elderly, atopic skin and heavy drinkers at higher risk. SNUH medical encyclopedia: low-temperature burn from 40 C+ over long time, no avoidance reaction, risk elevated with alcohol, sleeping pills, children and elderly, treat by removing heat and cooling with cool water, keep blisters intact, no folk remedies. NFA lithium-ion battery card news (2024-07-23): buy KC-certified batteries and chargers, never charge on beds/pillows/sofas, avoid humid places (short circuit), avoid heat and impact, unplug after charge, stop use and evacuate then call 119 on smoke/flame/swelling. Yonhap fact check (2026-09-30): Seoul power-bank fires 15 (2023) to 37 (2024) to 55 (2025), 2 deaths 5 injuries, about 277 million won damage; NFA battery fires 359 to 543 to 706; CISS power-bank hazard reports 22 (2021) to 136 (2024), about 6x in 3 years; charge within 4 hours, unplug before sleep or going out; swelling, white smoke, abnormal heat, smell and discoloration are thermal-runaway precursors. MOTIE KATS campaign (2025-11-10): do not store or use power banks in hot and humid environments. MOEL winter cold-illness prevention guide (2023-11-20): cold-wave watch at morning low -12 C or below for 2+ days, warning at -15 C; layer 3+ garments, warm hat, insulated gloves, warm shelter near worksite, rest periods during cold-wave advisories. KDCA emergency-room surveillance (2026-03-10 press release): 2025-2026 season 364 cold-illness patients (1.09x) and 14 estimated deaths (1.75x), hypothermia 79.7 percent, 65+ 57.4 percent, 6-9 am onset 20.9 percent, outdoor 75.0 percent vs indoor 25.0 percent. Japan Consumer Affairs Agency (OECD campaign R6-R7): 68 registered accidents (2014-2024) for lithium-ion warming products, 35 (51.5 percent) in heated vests/jackets, 32 battery-caused with 18 smoke/fire/overheat and 9 building fires, 13 during use and 11 during charging, including a vest battery that melted during wear. Peer-reviewed graphene heated clothing study (IJCST 29(6), 2017, verified via Crossref API abstract): 8 males at 0.6 C, intermittent heating protocol consumed 2.49 W versus 8.58 W continuous (71 percent saving), back heating more beneficial than chest for skin temperatures, fast-responsive graphene suits intermittent control. Ashde heated insoles manual (vendor): stage temperatures 40/45/53/60 C, warns of low-temperature burns from prolonged high-stage wear, recommends stages 1-2 for long use, wash after removing battery with cable cover closed using mild detergent in lukewarm water, no bleach or corrosive detergents, natural dry then reconnect, prohibited for infants/elderly who cannot sense heat. Product pages verified in-browser on 2026-11-02: Swiss Military HIVE-500S heated vest with battery 92,000 KRW (53 percent off 199,000), 113 reviews, 4.5 rating, only 4 left, seller Ivy Korea, product 8465886734-29152937395, Q&A confirms heating wires on the back only (none in front); Drone D-20000A power bank (fan-vest/heated-vest 5V2A dedicated, 20000mAh, 2 ports) 21,000 KRW (25 percent off 28,000), 109 reviews, seller Uniworks, product 8547915258-24752610828, seller answer states 5V2A in/out and no fast charging; Glenfield heated scarf SHS-01 with dedicated battery 26,500 KRW (72 percent off 95,100), 157 reviews, 4.5, nano-graphene film heating element, KC certification XU070671-22001A and EMC R-R-yjC-SHS-01, product 7043192553-17424926824, listed stages 42 C for 7-8 h, 48 C for 5-6 h, 52 C for 3-4 h on the dedicated 5000 mAh battery and up to 12 hours on a 10000 mAh bank. Affiliate short links freshly issued from Coupang Partners AF6593875 for all three ranks (ikWSTDHGIC, ikWWdEvJJJ, ikWX30RXPg); each link redirects to the correct product page with lptag=AF6593875 confirmed. Derived calculations recorded in research: cell energy 3.7 V x mAh, 85 percent DC-DC efficiency assumption, available energy 15.7/31.5/62.9 Wh for 5000/10000/20000 mAh, theoretical runtimes 1.6/3.1/6.3 h at 10 W continuous, 6.3/12.6/25 h at 5 W, 12.6/25 h at 2.5 W; cross-checked against KCA measured 4.5-10.5 h (stage 3) and 9-18 h (stage 1) and Glenfield 5000 mAh official 3-8 h figures. Plan deviations recorded: the plan's rank-1 candidates (Swiss Military/Nepa/Bodytouch carbon fiber 9-11 zone) were replaced by the verified actual bestseller Swiss Military HIVE-500S (113 reviews, battery included, in stock) because the listed 9/11-zone carbon-fiber models could not be verified as carbon fiber on the sales pages; the plan's rank-2 '20,000 mAh high-speed charging battery' maps to the verified Drone D-20000A whose seller explicitly states it does NOT support fast charging (5V2A fixed output is the correct spec for heated apparel, and the guide explains this); the plan's 'skin necrosis' claim in the Threads hook is softened to documented KCA/SNUH low-temperature burn outcomes (erythema, blistering, 2nd-3rd degree burns) since skin necrosis from heated vests has no official source; the 2021 test products are named in the guide as recall history while the mapped rank-1 is the current HIVE-500S model, not the recalled HIVE-310.
